category: A: identity resolution and the winner gate (MYEZ-001, 002, 003, 004, 011, 027 + owner report "the AI cannot spot products from the camera easily")
summary: I traced all three ways a comparison starts (camera, link, typed text) at origin/main 683f56c0. None of them can return "no winner". (1) Camera: one gpt-4o-mini call reads both photos and returns one flat list of up to 4 products. The route compares products[0] and products[1] with no record of which photo each came from. The vision `confidence` is dropped. A missing name becomes "Unknown"/"Unknown Product". Nothing checks the category or whether the item is a product at all. Product images are taken from the first search image for that name with no category check. The camera compare also passes no selected_category, output_lang, user_id or user_preferences. (2) Winner: deterministic argmax of `overall`. An exact tie goes to index 0. scoring_v2 pushes the loser's score down so the client never sees a tie. response_builder always emits overview.winner with a product_index. When there is no evidence at all, the factual verdict falls back to "X edges ahead on the overall picture." / "Y stays in the conversation as a close alternative." The only abstain-like guard (H6) fires only when specs and price are both None on both sides. The cross-category rule (Rule 1 in detect_comparison_quality) can never fire on the camera, typed-pair or link paths, because one pair category is written onto both products. On the link path the winner is simply GPT's winner_index under "Be DECISIVE" (default 0), with no scoring and an always-empty `recommendation`. (3) Build-3 client: it always shows TopMatchBadge, always styles one card as the winner (ties go to index 0), and only hides the RevealBurst animation for 'weird'. It has no state for "we cannot recommend". So on build 3 the only backend-only way to avoid a fake winner is to not deliver a result: camera `action:"error"` (Arabic visionFailed copy), or code INSUFFICIENT_DATA on text/URL (Arabic insufficientData alert). No existing ENABLE_* flag does identity or evidence abstention: GPT_WINNER only logs; HONEST_PARTIAL_SCORING nulls scoring_v2 on partials, but the client then falls back to winner_index and still crowns; COMPARISON_QUALITY_V2 only changes prompt text. Production flags recorded ON: CAMERA_FAILURE_ENVELOPE, PAID_ROUTE_METERING, COMPARE_AUTH_REQUIRED, COMPARISON_ID_ECHO. Every winner-related flag is default OFF with no recorded flip; HONEST_PARTIAL_SCORING's prod state is explicitly unknown. Proposed new dark flags: ENABLE_VISION_IDENTITY_V2, ENABLE_IDENTITY_ABSTAIN_GATE, ENABLE_WINNER_EVIDENCE_GATE, ENABLE_RESULT_STATUS_METADATA. Things to coordinate: SSE success:false still bills the credit (MYEZ-012), and the camera failure envelope maps INSUFFICIENT_DATA to the 'timeout' retry copy.

defects.id: CAMERA-SPOT (owner report: the AI cannot spot products from the camera easily)
defects.root_cause: Several code-level causes, all measured by reading the code; how often each one fires in production is unmeasured, since no prod logs were read. (a) One vision call takes both photos and is told to list EVERY distinct product, up to 4 in total. Products are not tagged with the photo they came from, and the route compares products[0] and products[1]. If photo 1 shows two items (bottle plus box, a background object), photo 2's product is dropped and the pair is wrong. (b) Model: the vision role defaults to gpt-4o-mini, and no record shows OPENAI_MODEL_VISION set in prod. It runs with detail:auto on a 1024px-wide JPEG made by the client, with no JSON mode. The prompt has no guidance for Arabic-only labels (GCC perfumes). (c) The output is parsed as a bare JSON array. A JSON object wrapper ({"products":[...]}) gives 0 products, and any prose prefix gives a parse error. Both end as action:"error" ("Snap each product in its own photo"). (d) The prompt invites guessing without packaging (shape/colour/logo, confidence=low). The returned `confidence` is never read downstream, so low-confidence guesses are searched as if certain. (e) A missing name becomes brand "Unknown" / name "Unknown Product", and that placeholder string is then searched on the web. (f) The schema has no category, no product_type, no is_product and no distinguishing features. (g) The camera compare passes no selected_category, output_lang or user prefs, so the user's chip cannot constrain the category and the prose is English. (h) The client UX gives contradictory guidance: needMorePhotos says "put both products together in one photo", visionFailed says "one product per photo". HEIC is detected server-side but rejected; this has no effect on build 3, because the app transcodes to JPEG.

defects.root_cause: Identity is never verified against what was photographed. Mechanism candidates (V04, two bottles shown as a watch and a violin): (1) per-image association loss and low-confidence guesses (see CAMERA-SPOT). (2) The product image comes from the first search image for the name, with no category or identity check: Knowledge Graph image, else the first organic image, else Serper Images[0], then GPT pick. A perfume line named 'Violin ...' can resolve to a picture of a violin. This is inferred for V04, since the result's dims ('leads on Versatility') show category_used was fragrances, i.e. the pair category was right and the cards/images were wrong. (3) The pair category is resolved once and written onto BOTH products, so a per-product category conflict cannot be represented. detect_comparison_quality Rule 1 (cross-category -> 'weird') is therefore dead on the vision, typed-pair and link paths. (4) The placeholder 'Unknown Unknown Product' is used as a search query, so search results for random items supply the images, prices and specs. (5) Nothing between identification and verdict checks that the resolved title or image matches the photographed category.

defects.root_cause: No identity gate exists. 'Unknown Product' placeholders come from openai_service (camera) and url_extraction_service (link), and they pass every check. _validate_renderable needs only a truthy name. extract_from_url returns success:true whenever the HTML was fetched, even with no title. The only abstain guard (H6) fires only when specs is None AND price is None on BOTH products; an empty specs {} or price {amount:None} counts as data (its docstring says so). The deterministic winner is a plain argmax; exact parity goes to index 0. response_builder always emits overview.winner.product_index and winner_index; scoring_v2 nudges the loser below the winner so a tie is never shown. On the link path (V09 is a Rasasi link) there is no scoring at all: winner_index is GPT's comparison.winner_index (default 0), produced under COMPARISON_SYSTEM's 'Be DECISIVE ... pick a clear winner' and 'NEVER return empty pros'. Build 3 crowns whatever index it gets (ties and null go to 0).

defects.root_cause: No evidence threshold before crowning. The winner is argmax(overall) even when every dimension is MISSING_SCORE or Tier-3-synthesized. The factual verdict has an explicit zero-evidence branch: when there is no price candidate, no rating candidate, no dim margin and no review-density candidate, line1 becomes '<winner> edges ahead on the overall picture.' and line2 falls back to '<runner> stays in the conversation as a close alternative.' The same 'edges ahead' string is the deterministic partial-verdict template used when the GPT verdict missed the hard cap (V10 shows exactly this string; V10 also showed partial-type symptoms). _partial_has_usable_data counts an empty specs dict as usable. The specs table rows include only fields both sides have, so an all-dash table means specs_comparison.rows == []. This signal exists but gates nothing. With ENABLE_COMPARISON_QUALITY_V2 OFF the verdict prompt always gets 'normal' (no hedging). COMPARISON_SYSTEM forbids an empty pros list and demands decisiveness, so the model invents generic reasons. A 2026-09-06 review measured that, at prod flags, a data-void product beat a measured unrated one in 9/9 categories (PO-RUBRIC-09).

defects.root_cause: The vision schema has no distinguishing attributes, and the prompt is label-OCR oriented ('FULL product name exactly as printed'). Two different shirts with only a 'GUESS' logo therefore come back as identical {brand:'GUESS', name:'GUESS!'} (inferred from V07). No code path detects that A and B are the same identity: there is no same-pair check in the camera route, the vision branch, explicit_pair, or the TextCompareRequest validator. dedup_brand_name does not collapse 'GUESS'+'GUESS!' because the next char is '!' (token-boundary check), so both cards read 'GUESS GUESS!'. dimension_winners are keyed by display NAME, so with identical names the per-dimension winner cannot be mapped back to an index. This gives the self-contradicting 'leads on Heritage' / 'pulls ahead on Durability' / 'The other product offers better durability' text. Identical search queries are extracted separately (in parallel, both cache-miss), so LLM noise in specs decides the winner (inferred).

defects.root_cause: Persistence and sharing carry no result-quality state. save_comparison stores any 'renderable' payload (2 named products plus metadata.query), so 'Unknown Product' rows and zero-evidence crowned rows are saved as finished decisions. The History list derives winner_index from metadata.winner_index or comparison.winner_index, which is always 0 or 1 because response_builder always sets it. Re-opening a row re-renders the stored full_response with the same crowned UI. The share endpoint returns the stored full_response verbatim. The client text share hardcodes 'Winner: <name>'. With ENABLE_COMPARISON_ID_ECHO ON (prod) the text-stream row is inserted before the terminal event. /home/savings sums winner-vs-loser savings from every stored row's winner_index. Partly mitigated today: camera unsuccessful results are not saved under metering ON. Link comparisons never reach History at all, because compare_from_urls returns no metadata.query, so _validate_renderable rejects them (V10's history row was a typed compare).

defects.fix_sketch: (1) The abstain gates (MYEZ-001..004) stop most bad rows at the source: an INSUFFICIENT_DATA body is not renderable, so it is not saved. (2) Under ENABLE_RESULT_STATUS_METADATA: stamp metadata.result_status, metadata.identity_confidence and metadata.data_coverage into the stored full_response. For any status other than supported_result, also stamp metadata.winner_index = None. history_routes already prefers metadata.winner_index, and the build-3 History list renders null neutrally, so this is a backend-only improvement for the list. (3) home_routes savings skips rows whose result_status is not supported_result. (4) share POST: refuse (409, code RESULT_NOT_SHAREABLE) for rows marked non-supported. Build 3 share sheet error-path behaviour must be checked first; otherwise only for 1.0.1. (5) 1.0.1 client: History and Share render a 'needs correction' tag from result_status; text share omits 'Winner:' when unsupported. No migration needed (JSONB field); legacy rows without the key keep today's behaviour.
defects.risks: Stamping metadata.winner_index=None while overview.winner and winner_index still crown inside full_response gives a mixed state when the detail is re-opened on build 3 (the list is neutral, the detail is crowned). That is acceptable only together with the abstain gate. The share refusal could surface as an error on build 3's share sheet, so verify the ShareBottomSheet failure path before enabling.

extra_findings.title: Link (URL) compare always ships an empty 'why we chose this' (explains V03 / MYEZ-017)
extra_findings.evidence: url_extraction_service.py:685 returns recommendation: comparison.get('recommendation',''), but COMPARISON_SYSTEM (extraction_service.py:1031-1060) has no 'recommendation' key (it is winner_reason). extra_findings.title: Camera INSUFFICIENT_DATA under the failure envelope renders the 'timeout / retry' state
extra_findings.evidence: ENABLE_CAMERA_FAILURE_ENVELOPE ON (CLAUDE.md:462) turns any unsuccessful compare into action 'comparison_failed', and ResultsScreen.tsx:338-346 maps every comparison_failed whose code is not in the outage set to setLoadError('timeout'). An identity or evidence abstain on camera must therefore use the pre-compare action:'error' (vision_failed copy) instead (measured).

extra_findings.title: Cross-category 'weird' rule is structurally dead on vision, typed-pair and link paths
extra_findings.evidence: detect_comparison_quality Rule 1 compares per-product categories (scs:1006-1009, _product_category scs:193-194), but the A3 write-back stamps category_used on both products (scs:4295-4296; url_extraction_service.py:641-642). The 'weird' off-ramp prompt (extraction_service.py:2085-2100) can then only trigger on a 10x price spread or, flag OFF, sparse specs (measured).

extra_findings.title: Vision JSON object wrapper silently becomes 'no products'
extra_findings.evidence: openai_service.py:213-222 iterates products only if it is a list. A model reply {'products':[...]} parses fine but yields [], so image_routes.py:412-421 returns action 'error' ('No products could be identified'). No response_format JSON mode is used (openai_service.py:187-194) (measured).

extra_findings.title: dimension_winners are keyed by display name
extra_findings.evidence: scoring_service.py:1677-1682 and 2633-2651 store winners[dim].winner = product_names[i]. Identical display names (V07 'GUESS GUESS!') make per-dimension winners index-ambiguous, which corrupts tradeoffs and key_tradeoff ('The other product offers better durability') (measured; V07 screenshot).
